keyCeremonyProcedure.description: Formal procedure for generating 5 operator keys with 3-of-5 threshold

operators.responsibilities: First responder for P0/P1 incidents, on-call rotation lead

participants.ceremonyCoordinator: Project Lead or designated Security Officer
participants.quorumRule: All 5 operators must attend ceremony — no proxy signers

preCeremonyChecklist: Air-gapped workstations prepared and verified (no network interfaces)
HSM clusters healthy and accessible from each operator's workstation
Video recording equipment set up (encrypted, access-controlled)
Data diode or QR transfer mechanism tested between air-gapped and online systems
Network isolation verified for all signing workstations
Emergency contact list distributed to all participants
Previous ceremony transcript archived (if not first ceremony)
BridgeLock.sol source code reviewed and hash verified by all operators

ceremonySteps.title: Pre-Ceremony Preparation
actions: Verify all 5 operators present (identity verification via government ID or pre-shared PGP key)
Distribute ceremony transcript sheets (one per participant, numbered)
Assign operator index numbers (0-4) if not pre-assigned
Verify HSM cluster health on each provider (connectivity, firmware, FIPS mode)
Test data transfer mechanism (air-gap → online) with dummy data
Verify network isolation: attempt ping from each workstation — must fail
Start ceremony video recording
Record ceremony start time in transcript
ceremonySteps.verification: All checklist items pass; all participants sign attendance sheet

ceremonySteps.title: HSM Initialization and Firmware Verification
actions: Each operator initializes their HSM session (PKCS#11 login, Azure CLI, or Vault token)
Verify HSM firmware version matches approved list (document in transcript)
Verify FIPS 140-2 mode is active (provider-specific check)
Enable audit logging on HSM before any key operations
Verify HSM has no pre-existing keys with label 'bait-bridge-operator-*'
Record HSM serial number and firmware hash in transcript

ceremonySteps.title: Key Generation (Per Operator — Sequential, Witnessed)
actions: Operator N generates ECDSA secp256k1 key pair inside HSM
Key label: 'bait-bridge-operator-N' (N = 0-4)
Key attributes: non-exportable, non-derivable, sign-only
Extract PUBLIC key only (never private key leaves HSM boundary)
Derive Ethereum address from public key
Verify key via sign/verify round-trip test on HSM
Record in transcript: operator index, public key hex, Ethereum address, HSM key ID, timestamp
Operator signs ceremony transcript page with their new HSM key
All other participants witness and initial the transcript entry
DESTROY any temporary files on workstation (shred -vfz)

ceremonySteps.title: Threshold Verification and Cross-Validation
actions: Verify exactly 5 unique public keys collected
Confirm no duplicate Ethereum addresses
Confirm no zero addresses
Test 3-of-5 threshold: sign a test message with operators 0, 1, 2 — verify all 3 signatures valid
Test with operators 0, 3, 4 — verify valid
Test with operators 1, 2, 3 — verify valid
Verify that ANY 3-of-5 combination produces valid signatures
Explicitly test 2-of-5: sign with operators 0, 1 only — confirm this is INSUFFICIENT for bridge execution
Compute and record the BridgeLock constructor argument hash
ceremonySteps.verificationCommand: Verify each signature with: ecrecover(message_hash, v, r, s) == operator_address

ceremonySteps.title: Contract Deployment and Registration
actions: Deploy WBAIT contract with bridgeLock address = address(0) initially (two-phase deploy)
Deploy BridgeLock with operator[0..4] = collected Ethereum addresses
Update WBAIT bridgeLock immutable address to BridgeLock address
Verify contract code on Etherscan (flattened source + compiler settings)
Each operator calls confirmLockMint on a test request to verify on-chain operator access
Verify 3-of-5 confirmations successfully execute a test lock-mint (testnet only)
Verify rate limit enforcement with test amounts
Verify pause/unpause functions work (owner only)
Destroy test request data (not valid on mainnet)
ceremonySteps.mainnetDeploymentDelay: Minimum 48 hours after successful testnet deployment

ceremonySteps.title: Ceremony Close-Out and Secure Archival
actions: All participants review and sign final ceremony transcript
Verify transcript contains: ceremony_id, date, all participants, all key IDs, all public keys, contract address, all signatures, witness attestations
Distribute signed transcript copies (one per operator + coordinator archive + auditor)
Archive ceremony recording (encrypted with separate key, access-controlled)
Set all HSM keys to production policy: non-exportable, non-derivable, audit-logged
DESTROY all temporary key material on workstations (shred -vfz, verify with hexdump)
Verify each operator's HSM key is inaccessible from other operators' workstations
Store contract address and ABI in shared configuration (bridge/hsm-configuration.json)
Start bridge monitoring (bridge-monitoring.py) for all operators
Send ceremony completion notification to all operators via encrypted channel

keyCeremonyProcedure.totalEstimatedDuration: 150 minutes (2h 30m) including 50 min for sequential key generation

rehearsal.description: Run full ceremony on testnet with dummy keys before mainnet ceremony
rehearsal.purpose: Identify procedural gaps, test HSM connectivity, verify transcript format

keyRotationSchedule.description: Regular key rotation to limit exposure window of individual operator keys
keyRotationSchedule.rotationPolicy: Rolling rotation — 1 operator every 30 days, full cycle every 150 days
rotationProcedure: 1. [T-7d] Notify all operators of upcoming rotation for operator N
2. [T-1d] Rotating operator generates new key in HSM (per key ceremony step 3)
3. [T-0d] Propose operator update on BridgeLock contract (triggers 24h timelock)
4. [T+24h] Wait 24h timelock period — other operators review replacement during this window
5. [T+24h] Execute operator update with 3-of-5 confirmations from OTHER operators (rotating operator cannot confirm own replacement)
6. [T+24h+12blocks] Verify new operator can confirm bridge requests on-chain
7. [T+24h+12blocks] Verify old operator can NO LONGER confirm bridge requests
8. [T+24h+12blocks] Decommission old HSM key: disable (set attribute CKA_ENABLED=false), do NOT delete — retain for audit trail
9. [T+24h+12blocks] Update ceremony transcript with rotation record (old key, new key, timestamp, confirming operators)
10. [T+24h+12blocks] Restart bridge monitoring with updated operator list
rotationChecklist: New key generated and verified in HSM
Public key address recorded in rotation transcript
3-of-5 confirmation transaction submitted by OTHER operators
Functional test: new operator confirmed a bridge request
Monitoring system updated with new operator address

emergencyRotation.trigger: Compromise suspected or confirmed for any operator key
procedure: 1. IMMEDIATE: Pause BridgeLock contract (owner action, < 5 min SLA)
2. Notify all other operators via emergency Signal group
3. Disable compromised key in HSM (set CKA_ENABLED=false)
4. If >= 3 uncompromised operators: Proceed with accelerated rotation
5. Generate new key for replacement operator
6. Propose operator update (24h timelock starts — cannot be bypassed even when paused)
7. Wait 24h timelock (bridge remains paused during this period)
8. Execute operator update with 3-of-5 confirmations from uncompromised operators
9. Verify new operator functional on-chain
10. External security audit of compromise scope
11. If audit clears: Unpause bridge with operator consensus
12. If >= 3 operators compromised: Emergency full contract migration required

sla.bridgeResumed: < 48 hours (if audit clear) or < 1 week (if migration required)

emergencyRotation.caveat: 24h timelock cannot be bypassed — plan for 24h bridge downtime during emergency rotation

disasterRecovery.description: Procedures for recovering from HSM failures, cloud outages, and security incidents

procedure: 1. Remaining 4 operators can still achieve 3-of-5 threshold — no bridge impact
2. Identify failed HSM (check HSM provider status dashboard)
3. Attempt HSM recovery (restart client, check firmware, restore from backup)
4. If HSM unrecoverable: Initiate standard operator rotation for failed operator
5. During rotation: Bridge continues operating with 4 operators (3-of-5 still achievable)
6. Replace operator within 48 hours using standard rotation procedure
scenarios.rto: Bridge: 0 minutes (no impact) | Operator replacement: 24-48 hours (timelock)

scenarios.impact: 3-of-5 operators available — threshold barely achievable, no redundancy
procedure: 1. Remaining 3 operators can still achieve threshold — bridge operational but fragile
2. ALERT: Bridge has zero fault tolerance — any additional failure halts operations
3. Prioritize recovering one HSM (fastest path to restoring redundancy)
4. If HSM recovery impossible: Initiate rotation for both failed operators (sequential)
5. Implement temporary heightened monitoring (30-second poll interval)
6. Require ALL 3 remaining operators to be available (no vacations, no maintenance)
7. Target: Restore to 4+ operators within 48 hours
scenarios.rto: Bridge: 0 minutes (operating at minimum quorum) | Full recovery: 24-72 hours

scenarios.impact: 2-of-5 operators available — CANNOT achieve 3-of-5 threshold — BRIDGE HALTED
procedure: 1. Bridge operations HALT — cannot confirm any new lock-mint or burn-release
2. Pause BridgeLock contract (prevent invalid state accumulation)
3. Notify all operators and coordinator via emergency channel
4. Attempt HSM recovery from backup (each provider has backup/restore)
- AWS CloudHSM: Restore from cluster backup (RTO: 30-60 min per HSM)
- Azure Key Vault: Restore from HSM backup (RTO: 10-30 min per pool)
- HashiCorp Vault: Restore from Raft snapshot (RTO: 5-15 min per node)
5. If HSM recovery succeeds: Verify keys, unpause bridge, resume operations
6. If HSM recovery fails for any operator: Emergency operator replacement
7. If >= 3 operators cannot be recovered: Emergency contract migration
a. Deploy new BridgeLock with new operator set
b. Migrate all pending lock/burn state to new contract
c. Verify state consistency
d. Update WBAIT bridgeLock address (requires new WBAIT deployment)
8. External audit of failure root cause before resuming
scenarios.rto: HSM restore: 1-4 hours | Operator replacement: 24-48 hours | Full migration: 48-72 hours
scenarios.rpo: 0 — L1 funds are safe (locked); no wBAIT minted without confirmations

scenarios.impact: Operators in affected region cannot sign — depends on geographic distribution
procedure: 1. Multi-region operator deployment ensures >= 3 operators in unaffected regions
2. Operators in unaffected regions continue bridge operations normally
3. Affected region operators: keys may be accessible via cross-region HSM replica
- AWS: Cross-region CloudHSM backup restore to alternate region
- Azure: Geo-replicated Managed HSM accessible from paired region
- Vault: Raft cluster auto-fails over to healthy node in DR region
4. If < 3 operators available globally: Pause bridge until region recovery
5. Monitor cloud provider status page for ETA
6. After region recovery: Verify HSM health, test signing, resume full operations
scenarios.rto: Depends on cloud provider SLA — AWS: 4h RTO, Azure: 1h RTO, Vault: 30s (Raft failover)
scenarios.rpo: 0 — no data loss; operations continue from unaffected regions

scenarios.impact: Bridge may be exploited — immediate action required
procedure: 1. PAUSE BridgeLock contract IMMEDIATELY (owner action)
2. PAUSE WBAIT contract (separate owner action — stops all transfers)
3. Assess vulnerability scope:
a. Can existing locked funds be drained? (check L1 side)
b. Can wBAIT be minted without proper confirmations?
c. Can confirmations be bypassed?
4. If patchable via proxy upgrade:
a. Develop and test fix on forked mainnet
b. External audit of fix
c. Deploy upgrade via 24h timelock (if using transparent proxy)
d. Verify fix on-chain
5. If NOT patchable (no proxy pattern):
a. Deploy new BridgeLock + WBAIT with fixed code
b. Migrate all state (pending requests, operator set, rate limit state)
c. Snapshot old contract state for audit
6. Resume only after external audit confirms fix
7. Post-incident: Bug bounty program update, monitoring enhancement
scenarios.rto: Pause: < 5 min | Patch: 24-72 hours | Full migration: 48-96 hours
scenarios.rpo: Variable — depends on whether funds were exploited before pause

scenarios.impact: HSM physical access may be compromised
procedure: 1. HSMs are tamper-resistant — physical access does NOT extract keys (FIPS 140-2 Level 3)
2. If tamper detected: HSM zeroizes all keys automatically
3. If HSM zeroized: Same as HSM failure — use rotation/recovery procedures
4. Report physical breach to HSM provider (AWS/Azure/Vault support)
5. Rotate all operator keys as precaution (even if tamper not confirmed)
6. Review HSM audit logs for any access during breach window
7. File incident report with physical security team
scenarios.rto: Bridge: 0 min (HSMs remote/cloud) | On-prem: 24-48 hours (full key rotation)
scenarios.rpo: 0 — HSM tamper-evident; keys zeroized on physical breach

azureKeyVault.method: Managed HSM full backup to secondary region

hashicorpVault.frequency: Every 6 hours (automated via vault operator raft snapshot)
hashicorpVault.command: vault operator raft snapshot save backup-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M).snap
hashicorpVault.additionalNotes: Encrypt snapshots with separate key (Shamir or cloud KMS). Store unseal keys separately from snapshots.

testingSchedule.description: Regular DR testing to validate recovery procedures

signingWorkflow.description: Offline/air-gapped signing pattern for bridge operator confirmations
signingWorkflow.securityModel: Defense in depth: HSM key isolation + air gap + multi-party threshold

steps.description: Bridge monitor detects new LockRequested or BurnInitiated event
steps.action: Alert operator of pending request requiring confirmation
steps.sla: Alert within 30 seconds of on-chain event

steps.description: Operator verifies request details on air-gapped workstation
actions: Transfer request data to air-gapped workstation (USB/QR/printer)
Fetch request data from offline copy of blockchain state
Verify: requestId is unique (not previously confirmed)
Verify: l1TxId exists on BAIT L1 blockchain explorer (offline lookup)
Verify: recipient address is valid Ethereum address
Verify: amount is within expected range and rate limits
Verify: Rate limit not exceeded for recipient (check dailyMinted)
Verify: No double-spend or replay attack indicators
Cross-reference with L1 explorer for lock transaction confirmation (6+ L1 confirmations)
For burn-release: Verify L1 address format is valid BAIT address (b'...)
For burn-release: Verify wBAIT was actually burned (check BurnInitiated event)

steps.description: Operator signs confirmation transaction via HSM
steps.system: HSM PKCS#11 interface on air-gapped workstation
actions: Construct confirmLockMint(requestId) or confirmBurnRelease(releaseId) calldata
Build Ethereum transaction (nonce, gas, to=BridgeLock, value=0, data=calldata)
Sign transaction hash with HSM-stored ECDSA key
NEVER: Private key leaves HSM boundary
NEVER: Sign arbitrary data (only known BridgeLock function calls)
Output: Raw signed transaction (RLP-encoded)
Log signing event in HSM audit trail

hsmCommands.azureKeyVault: az keyvault security-domain download --hsm-name <name> (for sign: use Azure SDK sign_data API)

steps.description: Signed transaction submitted to Ethereum network
steps.system: Online relay node (contains NO private keys, only broadcasts signed txs)
actions: Transfer signed transaction from air-gapped to online via data diode or QR code
Validate signed transaction structure before broadcast
Broadcast signed transaction via RPC endpoint
Monitor for transaction inclusion in mempool
Wait for >= 12 block confirmations on Ethereum mainnet
Verify on-chain event emission matches expected action (LockConfirmed or BurnConfirmed)
Verify transaction sender matches operator address

securityProperties.keyIsolation: Private keys never leave HSM — signing happens inside HSM boundary (FIPS 140-2 Level 3)
securityProperties.airGap: Verification and signing on air-gapped workstation; only signed tx crosses gap
securityProperties.nonExportable: HSM keys marked CKA_EXTRACTABLE=false, CKA_DERIVE=false at creation
securityProperties.auditTrail: All HSM operations logged with timestamp, operator ID, operation type, key ID
securityProperties.replayProtection: Each request has unique requestId; executed flag prevents double-execution
securityProperties.thresholdSecurity: No single operator can execute bridge actions — 3-of-5 consensus required
securityProperties.rateLimit: 100K wBAIT/day/address cap enforced on-chain — limits damage from any single exploit
securityProperties.timelock: 24h timelock on operator changes — provides review window for parameter modifications

operationalSlas.alertLatency: < 30 seconds from on-chain event to operator notification
operationalSlas.totalConfirmationTime: < 25 minutes from event detection to on-chain confirmation

auditLogRequirements.hsmAuditLogs: Retain for 7 years; tamper-evident; include all sign/verify/admin operations
auditLogRequirements.ceremonyTranscripts: Retain for 7 years; PGP-signed; include all key generation and rotation records
auditLogRequirements.bridgeMonitoringLogs: Retain for 1 year; include all event processing, alerts, and operator actions
auditLogRequirements.incidentReports: Retain for 7 years; include root cause, timeline, remediation, prevention

auditSchedule.internalAudit: Quarterly — review HSM logs, operator access, ceremony compliance
auditSchedule.externalAudit: Annually — full smart contract audit + HSM security assessment
auditSchedule.penetrationTest: Annually — test HSM access controls and bridge monitoring security
